name: Documentary Audio Intelligibility
source_tutorial: transcripts/what not to do in editing.txt
use_when: Dialogue, testimony, or location sound carries essential story information.
Train, street, crowd, wind, or camera audio is muffled or noisy.
Subtitles, dubbing, or narration repair may be needed to keep viewers from leaving.
Quiet words, clipped peaks, or uneven dialogue need volume keyframes before export.
avoid_when: The line is not important and cutting it is cleaner than repairing it.
Dubbing would misrepresent the speaker or feel more artificial than subtitles.
The audio issue is part of an intentional realism moment and the meaning remains clear.

timeline_pattern.priority_rule: Story comprehension beats decorative labels or lower thirds.
timeline_pattern.consistency_rule: If a B-roll sequence uses sync ambience, make ambience consistent across the sequence.

motion.rule: Keep graphics stable while viewers are trying to read subtitles or understand poor audio.

sound.rule: Bad sound is more damaging than bad visuals when the line carries story.
sound.repair_order: Try source selection, dialogue cleanup, volume automation, subtitles, then dubbing or paraphrase if ethically acceptable.
sound.mix: SFX and music must duck under critical dialogue.
sound.leveling_rule: Repair problem words with clip gain or volume keyframes instead of raising the whole track when only one moment needs help.

captions.rule: Subtitle essential hard-to-hear lines even if that means removing a lower-third graphic.
captions.avoid: Prioritizing a character intro graphic over the words the audience needs to understand.

color.rule: No direct color rule; keep visuals calm enough that subtitles can be read.

implementation.ffmpeg: Use loudnorm, highpass/lowpass, afftdn/arnndn where appropriate, and waveform review. Use volume keyframes/envelopes for quiet words. Render subtitle repair for hard-to-hear lines. Check dialogue intelligibility after music/SFX mix.
implementation.remotion: Add subtitle overlays for hard-to-hear dialogue and use audio gain envelopes around critical lines or quiet words.
implementation.blender: Do not add busy animation under essential subtitles unless the audio is already clear.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Use noise reduction, manual volume keyframes, and burned captions for hard-to-hear lines.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Use Essential Sound dialogue cleanup, manual keyframes, and captions; consider ADR/dubbing only when it is transparent and ethical.

common_mistakes: Assuming subtitles fully solve terrible audio.
Leaving a critical line unintelligible because a lower third occupied the space.
Letting music or SFX overpower testimony.
Using inconsistent ambience across B-roll sequences.
Raising a full clip when only one quiet word needs local gain.
qc: Can a first-time viewer understand every story-critical line?
Do subtitles appear for hard-to-hear speech?
Does music/SFX duck under important dialogue?
Is ambience consistent across related B-roll shots?
Would cutting the line be better than repairing it?
Are quiet story-critical words repaired without creating clipped peaks?
